documents.abstract: AI systems in human-AI teams must contribute to team cognition and elicit the correct perceptions in humans to foster adoption in critical domains. While prior work describes AI teammate roles that could benefit team cognition, human perceptions of these roles are underexplored. To examine this gap, we conducted a factorial survey where participants evaluated six AI teammate roles in four operational contexts for perceived usefulness, adaptability, performance and trust. We found that AI teammate roles significantly affect human perceptions, with the Process Analyst receiving more positive evaluations and the Information Translator receiving generally negative evaluations. Although context alone did not alter perceptions, it interacted with the AI teammate role to alter perceptions of trust and usefulness. These findings extend HCI and HAT research on perceptions of AI teammates, broaden knowledge on role framing to foster positive perceptions and highlight context as a critical moderator for perceived usefulness and trust.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Platform games offer a context for examining how character controller design shapes embodied interaction and player experience (PX). This study investigates how controller configurations influence operational behavior, strategic selection, and experiential outcomes over time. Using a theory-driven platformer prototype, four controller modules (restrictive, jump-focused, speed-oriented, and integrated) were tested with 48 participants in a within-subjects experiment. Data were analyzed using the proposed Operation–Strategy–Experience (OSE) framework. Results indicate that character controller parameters systematically drive distinct behavioral and strategic patterns. Operational variations evolved into strategic rhythms that mediated challenge, control, and emotional states. This study formalizes the OSE framework and advances the principle that constraint fosters creativity while freedom promotes exploration. These findings provide a temporal perspective on how low-level mechanics translate into high-level experiential progression and offer empirical guidance for optimizing character-controller synergy and long-term player engagement.

Introduction: Physical activity levels decline substantially during the college years, yet the psychological mechanisms linking social support to sustained exercise adherence remain insufficiently understood through longitudinal research. Grounded in Social Cognitive Theory, this study examined the time-lagged mediating mechanisms through which social support influences exercise adherence among Korean college students. Methods: = 20.3 years). Social support and baseline exercise adherence were assessed at T1 (baseline); exercise self-efficacy and athletic identity at T2 (2 weeks later); and intrinsic motivation and exercise adherence at T3 (4 to 6 weeks later). Time-lagged mediation was tested using structural equation modeling with bias-corrected bootstrap confidence intervals (5,000 resamples). Results: = 0.924). The total indirect effect was significant (β = 0.05, 95% CI [0.030, 0.073]), consistent with an indirect-only mediation pattern. Three significant indirect pathways were identified: (1) social support → self-efficacy → exercise adherence (effect = 0.029, 95% CI [0.013, 0.049]); (2) social support → self-efficacy → intrinsic motivation → exercise adherence (effect = 0.013, 95% CI [0.007, 0.021]); and (3) social support → athletic identity → intrinsic motivation → exercise adherence (effect = 0.004, 95% CI [0.002, 0.008]). Discussion: These findings provide time-lagged evidence that social support is associated with exercise adherence primarily through enhancing self-efficacy, which influences adherence both directly and through intrinsic motivation. Athletic identity contributed indirectly via intrinsic motivation rather than directly predicting adherence. The results support Social Cognitive Theory's emphasis on self-efficacy as a key mediator linking environmental factors to health behaviors, and suggest that interventions combining social support enhancement with self-efficacy building may be most effective for promoting sustained physical activity among college students.

Massive localized thigh lymphedema (MLL) is a rare, debilitating consequence of lymphedema, particularly prevalent in morbidly obese individuals. Its clinical presentation, often mimicking liposarcoma, poses diagnostic challenges. Surgical resection remains the primary treatment, accompanied by weight management counseling to prevent recurrence. This paper presents a detailed novel method of patient positioning in MLL resection. The authors describe the use of dual support candy cane stirrups, towel clamps, LigaSure TM , and a unique direct smoke evacuator to optimize access to the posterior medial thigh and the MLL. This paper also highlights the importance of recognition, dissection, and ligation of limb pedicle to prevent recurrence. The novel positioning technique facilitates efficient and complete resection of the MLL mass without complications due to better accessibility and support. The surgery for MLL resection can be challenging, thus we provide tips on a better method of patient setup for clearer accessibility to the field and a more streamlined method for patient and staff safety as well as surgeon ergonomics during the prolonged surgery. This paper underscores the importance of accurate MLL diagnosis and emphasizes the efficacy of surgical treatment. It introduces innovative patient positioning strategies to enhance MLL resection effectiveness and minimize surgical burden. As MLL prevalence rises with global obesity, healthcare professionals must be equipped with both diagnostic expertise and practical surgical techniques to address this challenging condition.

Maritime traffic complexity (MTC) is a term that has gained increased importance in the last decade in the maritime safety domain. It is a concept for understanding navigational safety and operational challenges in congested maritime environments. Although research interest in MTC has grown, it is a concept that remains fragmented, with various interpretations of definitions, indicators, and modeling approaches present in the literature. This study presents a comprehensive literature review and bibliometric analysis to synthesize the current state of research on MTC as a scientific construct and clarify its conceptual foundations from an analytical perspective. In accordance with PRISMA guidelines and systematic literature review (SLR) methodology, relevant studies were identified and screened across major scientific databases. A detailed analysis was conducted on 40 scientific publications. The findings indicate that most existing MTC models rely mainly on Automatic Identification System (AIS) data and corresponding derived metrics. MTC is primarily assessed through geometric vessel–vessel interactions, relative motion parameters, and collision-risk indicators. Bibliometric analysis demonstrates a rapid increase in scientific interest in this topic since 2015, with research concentrated in several leading journals. The study identifies a significant methodological limitation in current frameworks, which often overlook the heterogeneity of marine traffic, environmental conditions, vessel reliability, and human factors. Therefore, this study highlights the need for a more comprehensive MTC evaluation framework that incorporates operational, geographical constraint-based, environmental, and behavioral variables alongside traditional AIS-based metrics.

Embodied intelligent robots, as humanlike social actors, can rapidly comprehend users’ intentions and emotions in diverse environments from a first-person perspective and conduct real-time interactions while providing feedback on users’ needs. This study, based on the attachment theory, explores the influence of embodied mind perception on human-robot attachment. It suggests that perceived trust and perceived social interaction play a dual mediating role in the human-robot attachment relationship, and AI self-efficacy has a moderating effect. It offers a new view to deepen the understanding of the cognitive and emotional schemas, and enriches multiple perspectives for understanding the complex dynamic changes and their derived impacts in the human-robot fusion society.

The article examines the relationship between user experience (UX) and regulatory requirements in mobile application development, arguing for their integration as a unified basis for marketing and managerial decision-making. The paper analyzes modern UX-frameworks, ergonomics principles, behavioral technology-adoption models while systematizing GDPR, WCAG 2.2, and data-security requirements. The UX–Compliance marketing model of app development management is proposed in which UX and compliance jointly drive strategic, tactical, and analytical processes. The study demonstrates that such integration enhances user experience quality, reduces legal risks, and strengthens the long-term competitiveness of mobile applications

This study explores the classification of teacher attitudes and motivations toward implementing a Student-Centered Learning (SCL)-based curriculum in Timor-Leste using a neural network approach. Teachers were categorized into three groups: Proactive, Moderate, and Resistant. Proactive teachers exhibit a high level of motivation and positive attitudes, actively overcoming obstacles to implement SCL. Moderate teachers require additional support, such as advanced training or incentives, to enhance their engagement and adapt to the curriculum. Resistant teachers show scepticism and prefer traditional teaching methods, often due to a lack of confidence and resources. The neural network model demonstrated high accuracy in identifying these patterns, with intrinsic motivation emerging as the dominant factor influencing teacher readiness. The findings highlight the necessity of targeted interventions to address challenges faced by resistant and moderate groups, including comprehensive training programs, administrative support, and innovative teaching aids. Additionally, this research underscores the importance of fostering intrinsic motivation and positive attitudes to enhance professional capacity and adaptability. These insights serve as a valuable resource for policymakers and educators aiming to optimize the implementation of SCL curricula, thereby improving educational outcomes in resource-constrained environments.

documents.abstract: Abstract This study explores the dynamics of teachers’ stepping out of their established comfort zones in the contrasting contexts of advantaged and disadvantaged Turkish schools. Through doing qualitative analysis of the experiences of award-winning teachers (n=11), the research uncovers the multiple factors that either anchor teachers in their comfort zones or push them beyond it. Key findings suggest that a weak school culture, negative peer behavior, lack of vision from school leaders, and obstructive bureaucracy significantly contribute to maintaining the existing challenges and limitations in teacher development and school improvement. Conversely, high intrinsic motivation, a positive school culture, visionary leadership, high expectations from students and parents, and engagement in professional learning communities emerge as key factors in encouraging teachers to adopt innovative teaching practices. Limitations of this study include the study’s focus on award-winning teachers, suggesting further research to include a broader range of teachers.

Timely fault detection, classification, and localization are fundamental to enabling fast service restoration in modern distribution networks, and are especially vital for maintaining the reliability and resilience of smart city electricity infrastructures. A new AI-based method for classifying and localizing fault types is presented in this paper, which enhances situational awareness in smart distribution grids that supply dense urban loads and critical smart city services. The proposed approach targets various fault conditions, which include three-phase-to-ground, three-phase, two-phase-to-ground, two-phase, and single-phase-to-ground faults. The proposed method utilizes a wavelet-based signal processing technique to analyze the feeder’s current data captured by waveform measurement units (WMUs) and extracts features for fault analysis. As a result of these features, a multi-stage machine learning architecture incorporating deep learning components is developed to accurately determine the occurrence, type, and location of faults. To evaluate the performance of the proposed approach, simulations were conducted on a 16-bus distribution network. Results show a high level of accuracy in fault detection, classification, and localization. This indicates that the method can be a valuable tool for enhancing the resilience and intelligence of future power grids, as well as supporting self-healing and fast service restoration in smart city services.

documents.abstract: Vision-based human activity recognition (HAR) techniques have garnered significant attention and extensive research, with successful applications in many scenarios. However, their recognition accuracy deteriorates significantly under conditions, such as lighting changes and object occlusion. Considering that WiFi-based HAR techniques are unaffected by lighting conditions, we propose WiViHAR, a multimodal HAR method by fusing WiFi and vision information. Specifically, this method first utilizes atrous spatial pyramid pooling (ASPP) module and convolutional block attention module to design a dedicated deep learning network for processing WiFi channel state information. Concurrently, frame images are extracted and resized from vision, and the ASPP is extended to 3-D structure to design a dedicated deep learning network for processing the vision information. Finally, we concatenate the outputs of the two networks and apply the random forest decision fusion method to leverage the advantages of both WiFi and vision, enhancing the environmental adaptability of the method. Extensive experiments conducted in real-world environments demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms single-modal WiFi or vision-based HAR methods, achieving an accuracy of over 98.57% even under lighting changes or occlusions. This highlights the robustness of the proposed method, offering a novel approach for HAR fields.

Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools have rapidly permeated higher education, yet their cognitive consequences for working memory, cognitive offloading, and higher-order thinking remain insufficiently synthesized. This systematic review, conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, aimed to consolidate and critically evaluate empirical and theoretical evidence examining GenAI's effects on university students' cognitive functioning. A comprehensive search across six bibliographic databases covering 2023 to 2025 yielded 27 eligible peer-reviewed studies, appraised using design-matched quality instruments including RoB 2, AMSTAR-2, and MMAT. Findings reveal that unrestricted GenAI use measurably impairs long-term knowledge retention and critical thinking by substituting for the generative cognitive effort essential to durable memory encoding. However, structured, metacognitively scaffolded AI integration demonstrably preserves cognitive engagement and may enhance learning outcomes. Humanities students demonstrated disproportionate vulnerability to cognitive decline relative to STEM peers. Institutional policy frameworks, discipline-specific pedagogical redesign, and deliberate scaffolding strategies are identified as essential mitigating responses. The review concludes that cognitively informed, policy-guided GenAI integration represents the most defensible institutional approach, while urgent calls are made for longitudinal experimental research to establish stronger causal evidence.

documents.abstract: This article presents the development of a secure protocol and Android application for remote management of railway station security lighting systems. The proposed solution is basedon a two-tier security architecture combining application-level authentication using HMACSHA1 and transport-level encryption via TLS 1.3 protocol. The system implements multi-factorauthentication, including biometric methods (facial recognition), which enhances protectionagainst unauthorized access. The verification confirmed the system’s functionality and its compliance with modern security requirements for IoT devices in critical infrastructure. The developed solution contributes to improving the security and management efficiency of railway infrastructure facilities through process automation and minimization of human factor.

Implementation of an Injury and Illness Surveillance System at the 2025 Invictus Games Adaptive Sporting Event Ryan Murray, MAHSR, MD, CCFP, Lucas King, MD, MBA, BKIN,* Paul Dhillon, CCFP(EM), FCFP,† and David Jerome, MD, MSc, CCFP(EM)†,‡,§ Affiliations: *Department of Family Medicine, College of Medicine, University of Saskatchewan, Saskatchewan, Canada; †Department of Family Practice, University of British Columbia, British Columbia, Canada; ‡Division of Clinical Sciences, NOSM University, Ontario, Canada; and §Department of Family Medicine, University of Alberta, Alberta, Canada. Objective: To develop, implement, and evaluate the first injury and illness surveillance system used at the Invictus Games, and to describe the epidemiology of injuries and illnesses during the 2025 Games held in Vancouver and Whistler, Canada. Study Design: A prospective observational epidemiological survey. Subjects: A total of 534 competitors from 23 nations participated in the 2025 Invictus Games, which included indoor and outdoor adaptive sports. Clinical care was also provided to non-competitors including coaches, family members, volunteers, and spectators. Observation Technique: A paper-based Injury Reporting Form was designed according to the International Olympic Committee's 2020 consensus statement and STROBE-SIIS guidelines, with minor modifications for brevity. All medical personnel were instructed to complete a reporting form after each clinical encounter. Data were anonymized and transcribed daily into an online database for analysis. Outcome Measures: Primary outcomes were Injury and Illness Incidence Rate (IR; number of injuries and illnesses per 1000 competitor-days), and Incidence Proportion (IP; number of injuries and illnesses per 100 competitors). Secondary outcomes included descriptive analysis of patient presentations, including injury anatomical location, diagnosis, and interventions performed. Results: A total of 614 clinical encounters were recorded, of which 46.6% involved competitors. Among competitors, there were 286 clinical presentations, corresponding to an IP of 53.6 presentations per 100 competitors and an IR of 53.6 presentations per 1000 competitor-days. The highest IRs occurred in wheelchair curling (111.1) and wheelchair rugby (102.4); the lowest was in Nordic skiing (39.0). The most affected body regions were the head (22.8%) and back (21.5%). The most frequent diagnoses were pain (46.4%) and infection (30.8%). Most patients (90.9%) were discharged from on-site care, 20 (4.2%) were advised to present to the hospital, and 4 (0.7%) were transferred to hospital via ambulance crews. Conclusions: This study demonstrates the feasibility of implementing a standardized injury and illness surveillance system at an adaptive multi-sport event. The findings illustrate higher than expected injury and illness rates compared with similar competitions and highlight suggestions for improved pre-event planning and training, and enhanced reporting consistency. The surveillance data will inform medical planning for future Invictus Games and other adaptive sporting events. Edwards, MSc, MD, FRCPC,* and Pamela Weatherbee, BSc, MD, FRCPC* Affiliations: *Assistant Clinical Professor, Department of Psychiatry and Behavioural Neurosciences, McMaster University, Hamilton, Ontario, Canada; and †Clinical Lecturer, University of Calgary Department of Psychiatry. Objective: Athletes may experience a wide range of mental health symptoms, which can become disruptive or severe. Assessment may be required to determine suitability for training, competition and travel. All professionals working with athletes should be able to evaluate risk factors and identify safety concerns.Development of the Integrated Risk Model (IRM) supports continuum-based risk stratification, accounting for reciprocal influences between the athlete and the micro-, exo-, and macrosystem layers of their ecosystem, as well as relevant risk modifiers. The Athlete Risk Assessment Matrix (ARAM) enables longitudinal monitoring of risk, tracking improvement, deterioration, and trends over time. Data Sources: The first framework to guide clinicians in evaluating athletes' suitability for sport participation in the context of mental health symptoms and disorders was published in 2023 by Edwards, C. The model identified safety, stability, and function as key domains in assessing an athlete's suitability to participate in sports. Main Results: Recognizing that assessing risk and safety in sport is inherently complex, requiring consideration of multiple interacting factors. Consistent with the framework for assessment of safety, stability and function, mental health-related risk assessment of athletes should also be conducted within a framework or matrix. Risk assessments provide an opportunity to identify and modify risk factors beginning at the level the athlete, while also considering how adjustments within the surrounding socioecological contextual factors of sport (SECFS) layers may influence overall risk. Conclusions: Clinicians are encouraged to use the Integrated Risk Model (IRM) and the Athlete Risk Assessment Matrix (ARAM) to guide and structure evaluations of mental health in athletes. This article is in press (Advances in Psychiatry and Behavioural Health) and aligns with a priority area emerging from the updated IOC Consensus Statement on Mental Health in Elite Athletes (also in press). Ten-Year Sex Differences in Activity, Reinjury, and Quality of Life Following ACL Reconstruction Dana J. Hunter, MSc,* Denise Chan, MBT, MSc,* and Nicholas Mohtadi, MSc, MD, FRCSC* Affiliation: *University of Calgary Sport Medicine Centre, Calgary, Alberta, Canada. Objectives: To evaluate sex differences in clinical outcomes and patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) at 2, 5, and 10 years following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR). Study Design: Secondary analysis of a prospective, double-blind randomized clinical trial comparing surgical techniques with 10-year postoperative follow-up. Participants: Three hundred thirty ACL-deficient patients (146 females, 184 males; ages 14-50) with available data at one or more follow-up time points. Intervention/Observation Technique: Participants underwent ACLR within the original trial protocol and completed standardized follow-up assessments at 2, 5, and 10 years. Outcome Measures: Clinical outcomes include reinjury (graft rupture or contralateral ACL rupture) and osteoarthritis status (IKDC; coded as Normal/Nearly Normal or Abnormal). PROMs included activity level (Tegner, recoded as binary for <5 and ≥5) and ACL-specific quality of life (ACL-QOL). Results: Across 2-, 5-, and 10-year follow-up, adjusted linear models showed no evidence of sex differences in ACL-QOL. Female participants scored slightly lower than males at each time point (β: −1.45 to −3.87, all P ≥ 0.13), but effects were small and not statistically significant. Females had consistently lower odds of returning to high activity levels (Tegner ≥ 5) at all time points, with 52%–62% reduced odds compared with males (ORs 0.48-0.38, all P ≤ 0.015). Sex was not associated with ACL graft re-rupture or contralateral ACL injury at 2 and 10 years (ORs 0.75-0.98, all CIs crossing 1). However, females experienced a significantly higher odd of contralateral ruptures at 5 years (OR = 2.19, P = 0.053). Radiographic OA did not differ by sex at 2 or 5 years (ORs 1.41 and 1.19), and only a non-significant trend toward higher OA risk in males emerged at 10 years (OR = 1.57, P = 0.096). Conclusions: Sex was not associated with long-term ACL-specific quality of life, re-injury risk, or radiographic knee osteoarthritis up to 10 years post-ACLR. However, females consistently demonstrated lower odds of returning to high activity levels across all follow-up periods. These findings highlight persistent sex-based differences in activity participation after ACLR, while long-term clinical outcomes appear largely comparable between males and females. In order to increase the efficacy of education for adult learners of English as a foreign language (EFL), this study examines how andragogical ideas may be conceptually and intentionally included into English Language Teaching (ELT). According to the study, adult EFL learners require pedagogical models that take into account their autonomy, prior experiences, goal orientation, and need for meaningful, context-based language use. It is predicated on the shift from teacher-centered instruction to communicative and learner-centered methods. Knowles' andragogy provides a relevant multidisciplinary framework for reconsidering ELT in adult education with its emphasis on self-directed learning, experiential engagement, problem-centered instruction, readiness to learn, and intrinsic motivation. A convergent mixed-methods study was conducted with 28 graduate students from the ELT Graduate Program at Christian University of Indonesia Toraja. The educational intervention included four essential andragogical dimensions: problem-centered instruction, experiential learning, self-directed learning, and collaborative knowledge generation. Qualitative data was gathered through classroom observations, reflective journals, and responses from selected participants; quantitative data was gathered through pre- and post-intervention questionnaires that assessed learner autonomy, motivation, speaking ability, and academic writing. Learner autonomy, experiential learning, critical thinking, and instructional relevance all demonstrated strong results; however, students' involvement in selecting instructional materials and utilizing English in circumstances unique to their areas shown lower results. According to qualitative research, meaningful learning in adult EFL settings is closely associated with knowledge transfer, reflective practice, authentic tasks, multidisciplinary involvement, emotional significance, and technology-supported autonomy. The study concludes that rather than being merely an implicit classroom tendency, andragogy should be seen as a crucial theoretical framework for creating, implementing, and evaluating adult ELT. Andragogical principles can enhance adult learners' autonomy, engagement, and capacity to use English skills in social, professional, and academic contexts.

Accurate forecasting of respiratory virus-associated hospitalization rates per 100,000 population is essential for healthcare capacity planning, yet remains challenging during the COVID-19 era due to abrupt distribution shifts and symptom overlap among influenza-like illnesses caused by multiple pathogens. We propose a two-stage deep learning framework that disentangles stable pre-pandemic seasonal dynamics from COVID-19-induced excess hospitalizations. A lightweight GRU is first trained on pre-pandemic surveillance data to model baseline influenza/RSV-driven seasonality, after which an excess model learns from the residual series and integrates multiple online search trends (flu, COVID-19, and fever) using a standard multi-head self-attention mechanism. While we use COVID-19-era data as a case study, the proposed baseline–excess decomposition is not disease-specific and is intended to generalize to future large-scale respiratory outbreaks or pandemics that induce abrupt regime shifts. Experiments on U.S. weekly respiratory hospitalization rate data curated from CDC surveillance networks (AME) show that the proposed approach achieves strong accuracy on a chronological COVID-era split (2020–2025), reaching R2=0.907 with MAPE = 19.22%. Beyond point forecasts, we further evaluate an expanding-window rolling-origin protocol and report calibrated prediction intervals via split conformal prediction, supporting deployment-oriented uncertainty quantification. By decoupling baseline and excess components and fusing behavioral trend signals in a disciplined manner, this framework improves predictive performance under regime shift while providing interpretable excess estimates for timely situational awareness and healthcare resource planning.

Introduction: Metalcraft is a centuries-old tradition in Lalitpur, Nepal. Workers are exposed to various ergonomic and respiratory risks due to prolonged exposure to metal dust, fumes, and repetitive physical tasks. The present study aims to assess the pulmonary function and musculoskeletal complaints among metal craftsmen, particularly involved in making sculptors . Methods: A pilot cross-sectional study was conducted among 30 metal craftsmen purposively selected in Lalitpur Metropolitan City ward no. 6 and 17. Pulmonary Function Tests (PFT) were performed using a digital spirometer. Musculoskeletal discomfort was assessed using the standardized Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire. Results: 46.6% of metal craftsmen showed signs of respiratory disorders. Significant differences were found in % Predicted FEV1 and FEV1/FVC ratios (p < 0.05) between the different types of work in which metal craftsmen were involved. Lower back discomfort was the most common musculoskeletal complaint, but differences across work types and hours were not statistically significant. Conclusion: Occupational exposure among metal craftsmen may contribute to respiratory impairment. Musculoskeletal issues, although reported, were not significantly associated with work type or duration in this pilot sample. Further research with a larger sample is warranted.
